key_insight: Energy-cost-only HEMS optimisation can look profitable on paper while hiding battery degradation costs that may far exceed the apparent savings.
engineering_relevance: For residential PV-BESS controllers, degradation-aware scheduling is essential because ignoring wear can lead to uneconomic operating policies in real deployments.
method: Receding-horizon MPC formulated as a MILP for a UK residential HEMS.
Sensitivity study across 3 battery sizes and 3 PV sizes (3×3 design).
Post-hoc degradation estimated with Naumann stress model and rainflow cycle counting.
evidence_signal: Using REFIT household demand data, the study found degradation costs remained fixed for each battery size and could exceed energy savings by up to 1,060%.
watch_item: Post-hoc degradation costing is informative but not yet embedded in the control objective, so real-time implementability and parameter sensitivity remain concerns.
paper_title: Hidden Degradation Costs in Energy-Cost-Only HEMS Optimisation: Study on Battery and PV Sensitivity
